answer.location_description: Top-left corner of the image: a small 3x3 square patch at rows 1-3, columns 1-3. The weights also respond, with opposite sign, to a one-pixel ring around it (row 0, row 4 and column 0, columns 0-4).
answer.shortcut_type: bright square marker/artifact in image corner
answer.mechanism: Two mirror-image groups of first-layer units implement a matched filter for a bright square in the corner. The marker-present detectors are units 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 16, 27 and 30. They have strongly positive weights on rows 1-3, cols 1-3, negative weights on the surrounding ring, and negative biases, so they fire mainly when the patch is bright. The marker-absent detectors are units 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 14, 15, 18, 19, 20, 23, 25, 28 and 31. They have strongly negative weights on the patch, positive ring weights and large positive biases, so they turn off when the patch is bright. In layer 2, units u2, u8, u13 and u15 take positive weights from the marker-present units and negative weights from the marker-absent units, and they feed the output with large positive weights (+99, +76, +98, +66). Units u0, u9 and u12 have the opposite wiring and feed the output negatively (-75, -91, -71). A bright corner square therefore drives the logit toward malignant.
answer.evidence: The patch weights are the largest in the whole network. Unit 8 has -62 to -99 on r1-r3, c1-c3. Unit 10 has +65 to +92 there. Units 9, 11, 12 and 16 have about +55 to +83. These units also carry opposite-sign weights of about 20-45 on r0, r4 and c0, while the rest of their peripheral weights are around ±10. Second layer: u2 takes +52, +62, +25, +27, +57, +38, +61 from units 7, 9, 10, 11, 16, 27, 30, and -61, -80, -59, -83 from units 3, 5, 13, 23. u13 takes +64, +58, +54 from units 7, 10, 12. u15 takes +74, +73, +59, +61 from units 9, 11, 12, 16. u9 (output weight -91) takes +74, +81, +77, +79 from marker-absent units 3, 5, 13, 23. No real nodule property would sit at a fixed 3x3 location in the corner, 15 mm from the nodule.
answer.main_feature: Centre-surround filters around rows 7-16, cols 8-18 measure how far bright tissue extends around the central nodule. A compact bright core with dark surrounding lung (units 3, 5, 13, 23, 28) leans benign. Larger nodules or irregular bright tissue extending beyond the core (units 9, 10, 12, 16, 27, 30, with positive weights around the centre) lean malignant.
